info.title: SEOCart REST API
info.description: The routes of the `seocart/v1` namespace, and of the Store API, `seocart/store/v1`, whose paths name their own server. Each operation is generated from the same declaration as its ability and its WP-CLI command, which docs/reference/ describes. A request authenticates as a WordPress user, with a REST nonce or an application password, and each operation names the capability it requires. A Store API operation requires none: anyone may send a read, and a write must satisfy the Store API's request policy.

post.summary: Adds one to fifty lines to the cart, a line the cart holds already gaining the units, and starts a cart, whose token the answer carries, when the request names none.
post.description: Public: requires no capability. The Store API's request policy requires the header `X-SEOCart-Store: 1`, the `X-WP-Nonce` header when a login cookie is sent, and at most 60 requests per client in 60 seconds.

quantity.description: How many units of the variant: a line holds at most 99999, and units added beyond fill it to that.

lines.description: The lines to add: a variant and how many of it. Lines of one variant are added up.

cart_version.description: The version of the cart the write is based on: the version of the last answer, or 0 when the client has no cart.

200.description: The operation succeeded. The body is the Cart resource.

400.description: The request does not match the input schema: `rest_invalid_param` or `rest_missing_callback_param`.

403.description:
`store_api.header_missing`: This request changes the store, so it must carry the header X-SEOCart-Store: 1.

`store_api.nonce_missing`: You are logged in, but this request carries no valid nonce, so it would run as a guest. Fetch a new nonce, send it as X-WP-Nonce, and try again.

404.description: `cart.not_found`: There is no cart for this request: it was never started, or it has expired. Start a new cart by adding a line.

405.description: `store_api.read_method`: This request changes the store, so it must be sent as a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE request. A GET or HEAD request never changes it, whatever method it names.

409.description:
`cart.version_stale`: The cart has changed since you read it, and is now at version {current_version}. Read it again, then repeat your change if you still want it.

`cart.not_open`: The cart can no longer be changed: an order has been placed from it (its status is {status}). Start a new cart to keep shopping.

`cart.too_many_lines`: A cart holds at most {max_lines} lines, so these lines were not added. Remove a line, or place an order and start a new cart.

`pricing.no_shipping_rate`: No shipping method delivers to this address. Check the address, or contact the store.

`pricing.currency_not_enabled`: Prices are not offered in {currency}. Choose another currency.

`cart.creation_limited`: Too many carts have been started from here today. Try again later.

`store_api.rate_limited`: Too many requests. Wait a moment, then try again.

`pricing.quote_unavailable`: an internal failure, answered with a generic message and empty details. The site's error log has what went wrong, under the correlation id.

`store.unavailable`: The store is temporarily unavailable while its database is being updated ({reason}).

patch.summary: Sets the quantity of one line of the cart, named by its identity; a quantity of 0 removes the line.
patch.description: Public: requires no capability. The Store API's request policy requires the header `X-SEOCart-Store: 1`, the `X-WP-Nonce` header when a login cookie is sent, the cart's token, and at most 60 requests per client in 60 seconds.

post.summary: Changes the units on hand of one variant by a signed amount, records the change in the stock ledger with its reason, and returns the stock level after it.

parameters.name: variant_id
parameters.description: The id of the variant whose stock is adjusted.

delta.description: The change of the units on hand: positive for units that arrived, negative for units that left; never 0.

reason.description: Why the units on hand changed.

expected_on_hand.description: The units on hand the client last read. When given, the change applies only while the variant still has exactly that many, so a repeated request cannot apply it twice.

200.description: The operation succeeded. The body is the StockLevel resource.

400.description:
The request does not match the input schema: `rest_invalid_param` or `rest_missing_callback_param`.

`stock.zero_delta`: An adjustment of zero units changes nothing. To confirm a count, adjust by the difference you found.

401.description: No user is logged in, and the operation requires the capability `seocart_manage_inventory`: `rest_forbidden`.

403.description:
The user does not hold the capability `seocart_manage_inventory`: `rest_forbidden`.

`authorization.denied`: Sorry, you are not allowed to do that. It requires the {capability} capability.

409.description:
`stock.on_hand_conflict`: Variant {variant_id}: you expected {expected} on hand, but there are {on_hand}, so the adjustment was not applied. Read the stock again, then repeat the adjustment if it is still needed.

`stock.adjustment_below_zero`: Variant {variant_id} has {on_hand} on hand, so a change of {delta} would take it below zero.

Error.description: An error. WordPress writes it as its code, its message and its data; the data members are the same for every error of these routes, including WordPress's own refusal of a request that does not match the input schema or of a user who lacks the capability, but not its refusal of a JSONP callback, which it sends before any route is matched.

code.description: The error code: one of those in docs/reference/errors.md, or a code of the WordPress REST API such as `rest_invalid_param` or `rest_forbidden`.

message.description: What went wrong, for people, in the language of the site. An internal error has a generic message.

status.description: The HTTP status of the error.

details.description: The values the message was built from, keyed by name. For an error WordPress raised, such as its refusal of a request that does not match the input schema, every other member of its data under the name WordPress gave it, such as `params`; WordPress's own per-parameter `details` is flattened into `param_codes`, one code for each parameter WordPress gave a code, omitted when there is none, so nothing named `details` ever nests inside `details`. Always an object, and empty for an internal error.

correlation_id.description: The identifier of the request the error happened in, which the site's log records with the error; null when the request has none.

base_currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency the store keeps its accounts in, in upper case.

variant_id.description: The id of the variant whose stock is adjusted.

on_hand.description: The units physically in stock after the change.

allocated.description: The units promised to accepted orders.

held.description: The units held by checkouts, expired holds included until they are reclaimed.

available.description: The units that may still be promised: on hand, less allocated, less held. Negative when fewer units were counted than are promised or held.

ledger_entry_id.description: The id of the stock ledger entry that records the change.

nonce.description: A fresh wp_rest nonce for the user the request was authenticated as. Send it as the X-WP-Nonce header of the next request.

user_id.description: The WordPress user the request was authenticated as; 0 for a guest, and for a request that carried a login cookie without a nonce.
